title: Rav Chinena bar Idi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was a student of Rav Ada bar Ahavah, as in Avodah Zarah 40a, where he sat before him, and [Rav Ada bar Ahavah] sat and said — Hyman assigns the statement to Rav Ada bar Ahavah, against Seder HaDorot’s assignment to Rav Chinena bar Idi. He said to him: “From where do you have this?” He said: “From three verses; I heard it from Rav, Shmuel and Rabbi Yochanan.” In Pesachim 75a he asked Rav Ada bar Ahavah, who said to him, “The bread is permitted.” He said to him: “But did not Rav Chinena the Elder say that Rabbi Assi said that Rabbi Yochanan said?” Dikdukei Soferim’s reading, “But did not Rav Chana the Elder say that Rabbi Yochanan said,” is preferred by Hyman, for Rav Chinena the Elder was Rav’s student.

Hyman finds his words only in aggadah, as in Shabbat 63a, where he said: “Whoever performs a mitzvah as it is stated is not given bad news.” In Bava Metzia 59a: “Rabbi Chinena son of Rabbi Idi said: What is the meaning of ‘And you shall not wrong’? — one who is with you in Torah and mitzvot, do not wrong him.” Hyman suggests that perhaps he is the Rabbi Chanina bar Idi mentioned in Taanit 7a.

notes.text: Hyman explicitly assigns the Avodah Zarah statement to Ada, not Chinena; the saved Davidson40a context is retained as evidence without silently reversing his reading. The Chana/Chinena preference and only-in-aggadah observation are Hyman’s. עמיתך is expounded as one who is with you in Torah and mitzvot, not a whole people. Davidson English40a glosses the three verses as three great Sages and assigns the ruling to Chinena, against Hyman’s explicit preference for Ada; both claims are disclosed without importing the alternate role assignment into Hyman’s quotation.

The consulted Avodah Zarah 40a Hebrew leaves the actor compressed, while the Davidson English assigns the ruling to Chinena and glosses three verses as three great Sages. Hyman explicitly assigns the ruling to Ada; that reading and his Chana/Chinena preference are retained without silently importing the alternate actor assignment.
